summary.title: Moonlight Sculptor 01 · Before the First Bid
summary.description: Step into Lee Hyun’s evening at home. A treasured game character, a family to support, and one decision before bed. Book 1, Chapter 1 — opening installment.

summary.title: Moonlight Sculptor 02 · An Impossible Number
summary.description: A strange phone call. A number too large to believe. Follow Lee Hyun from disbelief to a new hope for his family. Book 1, Chapter 1 — second installment. Updated edition with a visible handheld phone during the call.

summary.title: Moonlight Sculptor 03 · The Price of Safety
summary.description: In a hospital room, the family’s new hope meets an old debt. Choose Hyun’s responses while the book’s events unfold. Book 1, Chapter 1 — third installment.

summary.title: Moonlight Sculptor 04 · Once More
summary.description: Three days after losing his fortune, Hyun finds a reason to stand up. A home to protect, forty million won to use, and a very unwelcome cancellation fee. Book 1, Chapter 1 — fourth installment.

summary.title: Moonlight Sculptor 05 · A Year Before the Game
summary.description: Hyun leaves the computer to prepare for a new world. A year of aching muscles, crowded walls and careful study leads him to Royal Road. Book 1, Chapter 1 — fifth installment.

summary.title: Props & fantasy actions · Rehearsal
summary.description: Try the visible phone, sword, bow and magical beam. An English-language animation preview, separate from the novel.

summary.title: Moonlight Sculptor 06 · The Price of Entry
summary.description: A year of preparation, an expensive capsule, and a familiar name. Step with Hyun into Royal Road’s character creation.

summary.title: 月光雕刻师 7：大家都在看我
summary.description: 走进塞拉堡，一切都像真的。可是，为什么大家都在看我？

summary.title: 月光雕刻师 8：只多了一点
summary.description: 别人看着，我一直练习。六个小时以后，终于有了一点变化。 Revised with continuous training, fitted reaction shots, and optional hall ambience and sword impacts.

summary.title: 月光雕刻师 9：休息一下
summary.description: 身体终于要休息，心里却还想练习。吃一点，再拿起剑。 Includes listener close-ups, repeated dummy strikes and optional hall atmosphere.

summary.title: 月光雕刻师 10：谁觉得没意思？
summary.description: 大家都觉得这样练习太累。一个骑士却说，这对以后有用。你听见了，也更清楚自己为什么还在这里。

summary.title: 月光雕刻师 11：还是太慢了
summary.description: 三个星期过去，新的本事出现了。可我一边开心，一边觉得：还是太慢了。

summary.title: 月光雕刻师 12：午饭的香味
summary.description: 面包快吃完了，教官的午饭却让三周的交情有了新的意义。

summary.title: Moonlight 13 — The Answer He Wanted
summary.description: A question over lunch. Hyun reads the instructor, chooses his words, and discovers an easy way to win approval.

summary.title: Moonlight 14 — Can You Carve Moonlight?
summary.description: A laugh about a moon-shaped pebble turns into a request. The instructor’s curiosity tests Weed’s easy agreement.

summary.title: Moonlight 15 — Two Silver Coins
summary.description: Weed hides his delight, accepts the instructor’s unusual quest, and receives two silver coins before taking a single step.

summary.title: Moonlight 16 — Please Leave
summary.description: Two silver coins promise a full stomach. But at the sculpture shop, Weed discovers that money is easier to count than goodwill.

summary.title: Moonlight 17 — A Welcome Worth Praising
summary.description: A golden two-headed eagle gives Weed a second chance. A few well-chosen words turn dismissal into a cold drink and an invitation to stay.

summary.title: Moonlight 18 — So It Was True
summary.description: Weed sees a poor business in beautiful statues. Then the shopkeeper confirms a story Weed thought impossible.

summary.title: One More Question
summary.description: A second quest draws Weed toward a royal secret. Better rewards sound tempting—until he reads the warning.

summary.title: The Price of a Secret
summary.description: Weed tries to pay a bard in compliments. The bard has another price in mind.

summary.title: The Promise That Remained
summary.description: A childhood promise survives separation. Weed doubts it could ever be kept—until the bard corrects him.

summary.title: The Sword in His Hand
summary.description: An eyewitness welcomes Weed—and remembers the moment the queen thought an old promise had been forgotten.

summary.title: A Promise in Moonlight
summary.description: The attendant reveals what Zahab made with his sword—and why the queen never forgot it.

summary.title: The Class I Refuse
summary.description: A fulfilled promise offers Weed a rare new path. His answer surprises even the system.

summary.title: The Gift I Cannot Refuse
summary.description: Zahab’s knife and a wooden statue are valuable gifts. The obligation hidden inside them has no cancel button.

summary.title: Back to the Wooden Sword
summary.description: Weed collects the silver he earned. Now another quest is tempting him away from the work he began.

summary.title: The Name of the Wind 01 · A Story Before Supper
summary.description: A quiet inn, five familiar guests, and a story interrupted by supper. Listen for what the innkeeper leaves unsaid.

summary.title: The Name of the Wind 02 · The Name the Wind Obeys
summary.description: A wall without a door. A step into empty air. And an innkeeper who suddenly knows more than he says.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 1: Who Is Speaking?
summary.description: Play as Jonathan, a Jedi on a new planet. Help a frightened girl find her mother - then discover why a familiar voice keeps calling from an empty room. Short Mandarin lines with audio, pinyin and meanings.

context.title: Episode I · A Voice in the Dry Season
paragraphs: Water is running low. Around a struggling settlement, every full container means another day of cooking, washing, and keeping a family alive. Jonathan, a Jedi far from familiar skies, arrives with An and the droid Q.

A missing child draws them into the streets. Before Jonathan can understand the settlement’s troubles, he must listen, ask for help, and decide whom to trust. Even a Jedi cannot solve every problem with a blade.

context.title: Episode II · The Last Door
paragraphs: The child is home, but the water shortage remains. Behind a closed water store, an unexplained voice has left Jonathan and his companions with questions. Answers will have to wait: the settlement needs a new supply.

Jonathan, An, and Q travel to Neri, where an aging depot may still hold the water they need. Others have come with urgent needs of their own. When machinery begins to fail, bringing water home may mean deciding what—and whom—they can afford to lose.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 2: The Last Door
summary.description: Travel to Neri for water. A failing pump traps Tao below: your preparations and decisions determine who survives, how much water returns, and whether An still stands beside you. Short Mandarin with audio, pinyin and meanings.

context.title: Episode III · The Water We Promise
paragraphs: The expedition to Neri is over. Jonathan returns with its consequences, and two communities are waiting for water. A storm is approaching; the pump that could sustain them tomorrow needs attention today.

The hill and river communities both want a guarantee. Min’s seriously ill wife cannot wait for a perfect agreement. There is time for only three preparations before the storm arrives—and a promise that wins help now may stand between someone and the water they need to live.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 3: The Water We Promise
summary.description: Three preparations before the storm. Balance lives, fair access and tomorrow’s water; your promises and preparations determine who survives and who holds power.

summary.title: The Player Who Would Not Take Gifts
summary.description: Four weeks with a wooden sword make Weed famous for the wrong reason. The more clearly he explains himself, the less the other players believe him.

context.title: Episode IV · The Line We Hold
paragraphs: The storm has passed. The communities must live with yesterday’s agreement, its promises, and its losses. Now a crack in the hills threatens the pipes beneath their homes. Jonathan and An set out to discover what has broken.

Jonathan wants something useful to bring back. An wants a partner who will listen when she says stop. Beyond the crack, a little water and an old diagram may offer a way forward—but bringing everything home could cost more than they expect.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 4: The Line We Hold
summary.description: Beyond the storm’s crack, Jonathan must learn when to hold on—and when to listen. Recover a sample, a route, or both at a cost. A story-led expedition with lasting material outcomes, without points.

context.title: Episode V · The Price of the Door
paragraphs: The storm is over, but the communities still live with their agreement, their losses, and the water they have left. Jonathan and An have isolated a damaged pipe. The evidence they carried home now points toward a western station that was supposed to be closed.

Somewhere inside may be the part their homes need. Yet a thing that looks abandoned may still be doing a vital job. Jonathan has learned to listen when An says stop. Now he must decide what bringing something home is worth—and who should pay.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 5: The Price of the Door
summary.description: At the closed western station, the part home needs is still protecting something. Carry your evidence forward, inspect before acting, and choose who bears the cost.

context.title: Episode VI · One Last Signal
paragraphs: The western station has given Jonathan and An a costly answer. Their part, their records, and their equipment depend on the choice you made. Any promise to repair the station door still matters. Now a red light shines from the northern tower.

A new storm is approaching. Travelers need a warning, and the tower has only one charged battery. Jonathan has learned to listen before reaching for a solution. Soon, listening may make saving a friend much harder.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 6: One Last Signal
summary.description: One battery, an injured friend, and travelers who have not heard the storm warning. What will your preparation let you save?

context.title: Episode VII · Who Owns a Voice?
paragraphs: The tower’s warning, An’s arm, and the navigation beacon bear the consequences of your last choice. The station door has been repaired where needed; lost records and equipment remain lost. A new lead points into the upper relay.

The voice asking for water belongs to a mother whose child is already safe. This time Jonathan brings her to hear it herself. Finding out how a machine speaks is only the beginning. Who gets to decide whether it speaks again?

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 7: Who Owns a Voice?
summary.description: Meet the owner of the borrowed voice. Follow the mechanism, listen to her judgment, and decide what evidence is worth.

context.title: Episode VIII · Your Own Voice
paragraphs: The repeated pleas came from recorded requests sent through dry pipes. Your choices decided the upper relay’s fate. Injuries, lost records, and damaged equipment remain part of the journey. A label points to a manual command from the eastern station.
Jonathan and An follow that lead. Somewhere beyond the empty pipes, a person chose to make those voices speak again. Finding that person may answer one question—and make the next decision harder.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 8: Your Own Voice
summary.description: Meet the operator behind the repeated voices. A confession, a control key, and three ways to answer for what happened.

context.title: Episode IX · What Remains
paragraphs: Ren has admitted ordering the recorded pleas to repeat. Jonathan and An promised to bring his own account home and settle responsibility for the eastern station. Their earlier losses, injuries and decisions still matter.

One question remains: why does water still flow through the closed western station? Before another journey begins, the people who carry these choices must finish what they started—and decide how to work together.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 9: What Remains
summary.description: Ren answers in person. The western water finally gives up its secret. Remember every loss and promise, then choose how to begin one shared future.

context.title: Episode X · The Strength to Stop
paragraphs: The voices have been explained and the failing western bypass is closed. Jonathan, An and Min promised to return together to repair the town’s supply. Earlier losses and promises remain part of the work.
At dawn, new maintenance parts await them. A supply ship is due that afternoon, and Min wants everything ready. But a stubborn connection will test more than Jonathan’s strength.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 10: The Strength to Stop
summary.description: Jonathan, An and Min begin the promised repair. A stubborn joint tests whether helping means using more strength—or listening sooner.

context.title: Episode XI · Before We Trust
paragraphs: The new connection is fitted, but the water valves remain closed. A repair that looks complete has not yet earned anyone’s trust. No drinking water has been used or created.
Jonathan, An and Min prepare an isolated test. The afternoon supply ship is approaching. They must learn what the evidence says before hope becomes another promise they cannot keep.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 11: Before We Trust
summary.description: The repaired line faces its first test. A disappointing result becomes useful evidence, and a small new delivery brings measurable hope.

context.title: Episode 12 · Hope Is Not Proof
paragraphs: The repaired connection holds pressure, but the drinking-water valves remain closed. Yesterday’s sealed delivery added two buckets; every earlier loss and agreement still matters.
The supply ship remains docked. Its crew will help clean and test the line today, while families wait for water they can safely drink.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 12: Hope Is Not Proof
summary.description: A missing label stops the final water check. Jonathan must defend a delay he hates.

context.title: Episode 13 · The First Water
paragraphs: Fresh, correctly identified samples have passed the ship crew’s water checks. The repaired line is cleared, but its valves remain closed until a controlled transfer.
Four measured buckets are ready in the ship’s potable tank. Jonathan, An and Min must bring them into storage, honoring the promises made before the repair.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 13: The First Water
summary.description: The tested line finally carries drinking water. Min discovers that keeping a promise begins with ordinary work.

context.title: Episode 14 · The Last Door
paragraphs: Four measured buckets have arrived through the repaired line. The water is safe, and the earlier allocation agreement still decides where it must go.
Jonathan, Min and Mother set out to complete the delivery. Bad weather is approaching, but a promise is not finished at the first convenient doorway.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 14: The Last Door
summary.description: A water delivery becomes a test of whether asking for help can be an act of trust.

context.title: Episode 15 · Stronger Together
paragraphs: The promised four buckets have reached their designated recipients. The delivery changed where the water is held; earlier agreements and losses remain.
Wind is rising around the exposed intake. Jonathan, Min and An have a new cover and straps from the ship, and a short window to secure them together.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 15: Stronger Together
summary.description: As the wind rises, three people must coordinate their different strengths to protect the repaired supply.

summary.title: Moonlight 28 · A Sword of My Own
summary.description: Powerful players offer Weed everything he needs. He refuses—and learns what four weeks of stubborn practice have really earned him.

context.title: Episode 16 · What the Storm Left
paragraphs: The storm has passed. The protected intake must be inspected, and the earlier deliveries, losses and agreements still stand.
Jonathan wants the community to return to ordinary life. Beyond the water station, a damaged learning centre is waiting for a careful decision.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 16: What the Storm Left
summary.description: After the storm, Jon wants a quick all-clear so the community can resume daily life. An directs a ground-level inspection; the water protection holds, but the learning centre's roof and furniture need work. Jon stops treating speed as proof of competence. They agree to reopen the centre only after trained inspection and repair.

intro.title: A Place to Come Back To

context.title: Episode 17 · A Place to Come Back To
paragraphs: The water protection has held. The damaged learning centre remains closed while qualified repairs are arranged; temporary classes will meet in a separately inspected safe space.
Mother is helping families return. A teacher named Sela and a parent named Ivo have different ideas about what a child needs to bring back to school.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 17: A Place to Come Back To
summary.description: The centre's teacher, introduced as a new resident rather than a replacement for anyone lost, wants displaced learners to return. A parent worries that absences and old report cards will humiliate their son. Mother helps arrange temporary classes and companionship. The teacher listens before setting the return plan; An contributes without lifting or climbing.

context.title: Episode 18 · The Test That Helps
paragraphs: The damaged learning centre remains closed. A separately inspected courtyard is ready for temporary lessons; earlier losses, promises and water allocations still stand.
Jon has offered to help Sela teach. He has prepared a tiny bridge, two paper animals and rather more confidence than the lesson requires.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 18: The Test That Helps
summary.description: Jon offers an overconfident demonstration at the temporary class. A teacher helps him turn a confusing exercise into a useful test of how people learn: simple physical models, translated labels, and a short illustrated story with a bear's paw and a wolf. His awkward demonstration earns a laugh; he learns to ask what the learners need rather than show what he knows.

context.title: Episode 19 · Who Gets to Apply?
paragraphs: Temporary lessons have produced clear instructions for the learning centre. The roof still needs qualified repairs, and the community is recruiting paid staff.
An applicant from another settlement arrives before the deadline with practical experience and a paper resume. The application terminal has stopped working.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 19: Who Gets to Apply?
summary.description: A community hiring notice offers paid maintenance and centre-support work. A new applicant from another settlement has useful experience but no prestigious qualification. A broken application terminal and a dismissive gatekeeper threaten to exclude them. Jon and Min insist on a paper alternative and a relevant practical assessment.

context.title: Episode 20 · A Fair Trial
paragraphs: Applications have been accepted fairly. Ryn’s preliminary assessment is complete, but references and a formal interview still stand between the crew and paid repair work.
The learning centre remains closed. Min wants a fair decision and a quick reopening; looking important may be easier than making a responsible promise.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 20: A Fair Trial
summary.description: Candidates face a supervised practical interview. One assessor judges clothes and confidence instead of competence; another wants unpaid overtime to rush the opening. Min, sensitive about his own reputation, backs a fair skills test and written paid trial terms. The group rejects appearance-based selection and sets realistic staffing limits.

context.title: Episode 21 · Leave Room for the Bees
paragraphs: A qualified repair crew has accepted clear paid terms. The damaged learning centre remains closed, while the teaching garden needs a safe route and affordable supplies.
Jon is ready to clear the path. A small nest near the old route will test whether being protective always means taking action.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 21: Leave Room for the Bees
summary.description: The crew clears the centre's neglected teaching garden. Jon mistakes a nest near the path for an enemy to remove. A knowledgeable gardener redirects the group before anyone rushes at it or strikes the insects. They cordon off the area and work on a safe section, learning why flowers and pollinators matter to the community.

context.title: Episode 22 · What the Stall Is For
paragraphs: The garden has a safe alternate path. Its old path remains closed, and the learning centre still needs repairs before children can return.
Min and a local cook are raising money for agreed supplies. Jon arrives ready to make the occasion grand; a small bowl of soup may change his plans.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 22: What the Stall Is For
summary.description: Min and a resident cook run a small food stall to fund approved centre supplies. Jon imagines a grand feast, then discovers that prices, portions and ordinary soup matter more. A customer challenges an exaggerated honey advertisement; the cook removes its weight-loss and calming claims. They choose a shared meal and transparent accounts over prestige.

context.title: Episode 23 · A Promise Worth Believing
paragraphs: The courtyard stall has raised a recorded budget for essential supplies. Qualified workers are ready, but the learning centre is still closed.
A vendor offers a quick solution and a gleaming improvement. Jon must decide what makes a promise worth trusting—and explain it to someone who is listening.

summary.title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 23: A Promise Worth Believing
summary.description: A confident vendor promises an instant repair and tries to sell a decorative upgrade as essential. Jon notices a clever use of true details to hide a false promise. A learner's question from a philosophy reading forces him to explain his reasoning plainly. The crew checks evidence, refuses the offer and uses the agreed budget for necessary materials.

intro.title: Do you want to see my scar?

summary.title: Super Supportive · Episode 1: Someone Who Answers
summary.description: Two weeks after the disaster, young Alden receives a visitor. A small, unexpected conversation gives him something he has been missing: someone who takes his questions seriously.
